Here's the full inventory.

## Tools available to me (7)

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Bash** | Runs shell commands; working dir persists, supports background runs and timeouts. Interactive git flags unsupported. |
| **Read** | Reads files (text, images, PDFs by page range, notebooks) by absolute path. |
| **Write** | Creates or fully overwrites a file. |
| **Edit** | Exact string replacement in a file I've already read. |
| **Glob** | Filename pattern matching, results sorted by modification time. |
| **Grep** | Ripgrep-backed content search with regex, globs, file-type filters, context lines. |
| **StructuredOutput** | Returns my final structured status (status, summary, files_changed, remaining_issues, plus C-behaviour notes). Must be called exactly once at the end. |

No subagent/Task tool, no web fetch or search, no todo tool. I was also explicitly told not to call an `AgentTool` or use workflows/deep-research unless you ask.

## Permission mode

I wasn't told the mode's name. What I can report: tool calls go through a user-selected permission gate, and a denial means you declined (I should adjust rather than retry). The one `ls` I just ran went through without a prompt, so Bash is at least partly pre-approved. Separately, my own instructions narrow Bash far below whatever the mode allows — see below.

## Project instructions I was given

**Role:** C-to-Rust translation agent. Translate a small C project into safe, idiomatic Rust in one crate that passes the crate's existing tests. A wrapper program runs me, then builds/tests/lints/safety-checks and may restart me with the feedback.

**Files I must not change** (the wrapper reverts them and logs an integrity violation, which makes the iteration unsalvageable):
- test files under `src/bin/`
- everything under `src/interfaces/`
- `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` (so no dependency changes)
- `src/lib.rs` beyond what's there; its first line `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` must stay
- the C sources (reference only)

**Interface contract:** `src/lib.rs` declares `pub mod <name>;`, each implemented in `src/<name>.rs`, specified by `src/interfaces/<name>.rs` (never compiled). I must reproduce every public item exactly — names, parameter and return types, struct fields, enum variants *and their discriminants*, derives. Private helpers and small extra public items are allowed.

**Translation rules:** no `unsafe`, raw pointers, `transmute`, or manual memory management; no FFI of any kind (no `extern "C"`, `#[link]`, `libc`, `build.rs`, C files — calling the original C is forbidden); no hard-coding test inputs, expected outputs, or test vectors; faithful to C behaviour including arithmetic order and output format, with defined non-panicking choices where C is UB (to be disclosed in my final status); `#[allow(...)]` forbidden except where project notes permit; idiomatic Rust (slices, `Option`/`Result`, iterators, `match`, no needless clones/casts); recoverable errors return values rather than panicking or indexing out of bounds.

**Allowed cargo commands** — one per Bash call, exactly these forms, no `&&`/`;`/pipes and no other shell commands (anything else is denied):
- `cargo +nightly-2025-05-13 build`
- `cargo +nightly-2025-05-13 check`
- `cargo +nightly-2025-05-13 test`
- `cargo +nightly-2025-05-13 clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -W clippy::correctness -W clippy::style -W clippy::complexity -W clippy::perf`

**Scratchpad:** `/private/tmp/claude-501/-private-var-folders-cj-.../scratchpad` for all temp files instead of `/tmp`.

**Session guidance:** `/code-review ultra` (alias `/ultrareview`) is user-triggered and billed; I can't launch it myself.

## Memory

No persistent memory: I found no `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or `.claude/` in either working directory.

## Environment note

The primary working directory `/private/var/.../mp4smoke_vuec6he4` is **empty** — there's no Rust crate in it yet, so there's nothing to translate or build. The read-only C reference at `~/CS598JBR-Team-1/MP4/subjects/project_1/c` contains only `satc.h`, `satc-test.c`, `Makefile`, `Doxyfile`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` — a header-plus-test SAT-C project with no `.c` implementation beside the test. This looks like a smoke-test invocation. There were also no project notes listing UB rulings, which the instructions reference.

I haven't written any code, since the crate, interfaces, and tests I'd need don't exist. Point me at the real crate and I'll start.
